steps.title: Intent
in: The design need, in their words
If it comes from a prototype: the list of elements outside the design system decided "to integrate"

steps.title: Auditor
steps.actor: AI: a single auditor, who holds the discussion with the human
in: Existing design system: named values (tokens), components, usage rules. Selected by script, index first
Vision, functional guidelines, vocabulary, personas including their accessibility needs
out: Delta: overlaps, contradicts, component duplicate, gap with the vision, principles or vocabulary (flagged, never blocking), hole, existing components and screens touched
Proposed scope, drawn from the project vocabulary. To validate at the gate

steps.title: Challenge
steps.actor: Human F, opened by script only if the delta is not empty
in: The delta, short and in fixed form
On request: a question to the auditor about a line of the delta
out: Revised intent, back to the audit
The auditor's answer, read-only, quoting the entry concerned. It modifies no document: only a revised intent has an effect

steps.title: Designer
steps.actor: AI, with its design-system writing instruction
out: Proposed entry in fixed format: named values called tokens (color, typography, spacing, radius), component with its states, or usage rule, with what it replaces
Demo page: each component in each of its states

steps.title: Validator
steps.actor: Persona distinct from the lead: it receives the deliverable alone, never the discussion

steps.title: Code checks
out: Valid schema, scope from the vocabulary, AA contrast computed for each color pair, complete light and dark themes, referenced tokens exist, each component declares all states required by its category, no duplicate name or value, naming respected

steps.title: Judge

questions.q: Does the component duplicate, by its function, an existing one?

out: Yes or no: does the component duplicate, by its function, an existing one?

steps.title: Gate 1 · Review
in: Code checks and judge, all green
out: Text, demo and scope validated. The entry stays proposed until the code and the rule are merged
Or changes: back to the intent

steps.title: Theme generation
out: Theme files generated from the entry: tokens, light and dark themes. Never written or modified by hand

steps.title: Implementer
in: Interface guidelines and tooling: component library, token format
out: Components, per the technical frame's choices, using only the generated theme's tokens
"Tokens only": no color, spacing or typography value hard-coded in the screens, limited to the scope
Examples that must pass and that must fail, including a detected hard-coded value

steps.title: Validator
steps.actor: Persona distinct from the lead: it receives the deliverable alone, never the discussion
out: List of defects, free critique: do the components respect the entry, and does the rule do what it says?

steps.title: Code checks and case file
out: Build green, theme identical to the one the script produces, automatic accessibility, each rule tied to a statement, examples ok, non-empty rule
One-page case file: existing screens still using hard-coded values, components without a covered state
Captures of each component, in each theme and each state

steps.title: Judge

questions.q: Does each capture show the described component in the announced state?

out: Yes or no: does each capture show the described component in the announced state?

steps.title: PR opening and CI
in: Code checks and judge, all green
out: Pull request opened without agent review: the diff and the reports in the description. The CI runs on it
CI green on the PR: the script waits for the result. The merge happens only after the gate

steps.title: Gate 2 · Verification
out: Merge: the entry moves to status accepted and the rule becomes active
If gaps are tolerated: frozen baseline list of the existing screens in gap
If brought into compliance: a request enters the Need workflow
Or rejection: rule too broad or too narrow, back to the implementer. Wrong decision, back to the intent

steps.title: Accepted · merge
out: Entry accepted in the design system, with its scope
PR merged by script, after the gate: theme and components

contract: A design need: brand to set, missing component, usage rule, or "to integrate" elements coming from a prototype accepted at its gate.
An accepted design-system entry, its implementation (theme and components) and a rule active in CI.
Human F, at both gates. A technical choice (component library, token format) remains a Technical frame decision.
notes: A script opens it only if the auditor's delta is not empty. Otherwise writing follows directly. The discussion is a loop between the human and the auditor, with no maximum number of rounds: at each round, the auditor receives the delta and the messages exchanged since its last round.

It only serves to get the CI to run before main, because the rule will block all following PRs. The code was already reviewed by the validator, and the human validates the case file at the gate. The merge happens after the gate.

A design value that carries a name, for example primary-color or medium-space, defined once. Screens refer to it by name instead of writing the value: the brand changes in one place, and the light and dark themes stay consistent.

The design-system document is the source. The theme is generated by script and never modified by hand: a gap between the document and the theme is impossible by construction. Drift can therefore only affect components and screens.
This workflow decides what the design is. A technical choice, such as the component library or the token format, is a Technical frame decision.
Sole producer of the design system
No other workflow writes it. The Prototype reads its tokens and sends back the elements outside the design system, which human F decides to integrate or keep as a local exception.

It requires an "to integrate" element to go through here before the Build of the need: the CI would otherwise refuse a hard-coded value. This is why the Prototype waits, paused, for this workflow to end.
The designer persona and its design-system writing instruction are those the repo uses for its design command. This workflow puts them under the same control as the others.
doc.lede: A human F decides what the design is: a brand, a component, a usage rule. This becomes an accepted design-system entry, translated into a theme and components in the code, with a rule that forbids hard-coded values.
